title: The Shortening Ladder
hints: Closures can drop their types, `return` and parameter names (`$0`).
Filter the names starting with "t" (case-insensitive), then sort by a tuple of (length, name).
jsBridge: Swift's closure-shortening ladder: full syntax → inferred types → implicit return → `$0`/`$1` → trailing closure. JS arrow functions sit at about step 3. `$0` has no JS equivalent, though Kotlin's `it` is close.

Why can't you use `$0` inside a nested closure to mean the outer closure's argument?
